0.original: Seigetsu the Enlightened is concerned about the clash of cultures.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※Please note that the difficulty of this quest has been synced to your current level. Furthermore, you may not proceed with a class or job that is different from when you accepted this quest.

25.original: Ride a mikoshi to the Dusk Throne and use the Wasshoi ability at the designated location.

26.original: Ride a mikoshi to the Dawn Throne and use the Wasshoi ability at the designated location.

48.original: It is an unfortunate fact that whilst the collision of cultures is often an enriching affair for all concerned, a sudden encounter with the unfamiliar can just as easily lead to conflict. As such, we cannot assume that the Xaela will accept us with open arms.

49.original: No, should matters come to blows, those proud warrior people could have every one of us steamed and served in a buuz─in the most disturbingly literal fashion─which would put quite a damper on efforts to refine our civilization.

50.original: Thus did I bend my intellect to the task of how we might avoid such an unpleasant fate. After much deliberation, I was rewarded with the most ingenious idea: we shall exhibit our peaceful intentions to the Xaela by paying our respects to their gods!

51.original: Go now, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>! Gyotaku will provide you with a mikoshi, that you might float with serene purpose to the sacred sites of the Azim Steppe.

52.original: A number of my kin have already begun their pilgrimage, and await your arrival at the Dusk Throne. When the Xaela witness <hex:021A020203>you<hex:021A020103> leading the devotions of our people from atop the mikoshi, they will surely recognize the harmonious significance of your presence!

53.original: You have come for a mikoshi, yes, yes? Hop on board, and honor those Xaela gods with a rousing Namazu wasshoi!

54.original: When the others returned with the mikoshi, I had thought your mission successfully completed. But it seems you simply hopped down...or tumbled off. Here, why don't you try again, and keep a tighter grip this time, yes, yes?

55.original: Dusky goddess, we come to offer our respects! We hope our display of worship meets with your approval!

56.original: I wonder if the goddess minds being buried in the sand like that... A Namazu would just dry right out! Shrivel right up! We'll have to continue our visits and keep Her company!

57.original: The goddess is so <hex:021A020203>expansive<hex:021A020103>, the way Her magnificence fills your vision... I felt an itch in my fins to just start climbing and nestle myself i─ Hm? Of course I didn't clamber up this sacred statue! No, no!

58.original: Our duty is done. Your wasshoi was wonderful, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>! Most devotional! Now we must present ourselves at the Dawn Throne. See you there, yes? Yes, yes!

59.original: Do not be alarmed─we are the Namazu from atop the Towering Still! We have put aside our festival preparations to come before the gods of the Azim Steppe and pay the proper obeisance!

60.original: As our friend here has demonstrated from atop the mikoshi, a spirited wasshoi is the Namazu way of showing respect!

61.original: I might think you come to insult us...but if the champion of the Naadam acts on your behalf, then we must accept the sincerity of your words.

62.original: Thank you for accompanying these...envoys. I saw only finned creatures flapping towards us, and thought catfish had dragged themselves up from the Azim Khaat. I was close to kicking them into the water...

63.original: Seigetsu the Enlightened has ordered─very firmly suggested─that we perform our greetings on a regular basis. And so here we are!

64.original: Gods and mortals, natives and visitors alike, may we all be filled with festive spirit!

65.original: Again, you come. Again we struggle to understand your ways. And again we will recognize your efforts to show respect, as odd as they are...

66.original: These <hex:021A020203>unique<hex:021A020103> displays of worship have captured the attention of many of our people. The Namazu are fortunate you chose to participate─they might otherwise have been seen as a threat, rather than a confusing curiosity.

67.original: And now we must return to our tasks. Peace be with you! And with you, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>!

68.original: We, too, must return to our duties. Know that you are welcome to approach again should you wish to entertai─ahem, “honor” us with another show of respect.

70.original: We are but humble Namazu! Bear witness as we demonstrate our respect for your mighty deities!

71.original: The Namazu have approached the Oronir. Speak with Gyotaku at Dhoro Iloh to mount a mikoshi, and perform a rousing Wasshoi before the Dawn Throne.

72.original: We're ready for the wasshoi now. Let's make it a good one!

73.original: The Namazu are waiting to perform their greeting alongside the mikoshi. Speak with Gyotaku at Dhoro Iloh to mount a mikoshi, and perform a rousing Wasshoi before the Dusk Throne.

74.original: I thank you for leading our people in the pursuit of harmony. Tell me, were the Xaela receptive to our overtures?

75.original: Ah, just as I suspected: your presence is essential for fostering an atmosphere of acceptance, if not outright trust. The mutual understanding gained through the exchange of cultures is truly a marvelous thing, and it is a road that we must continue to pave if we would improve our civilization.
